sections.heading: Hero
sections.body: A technical limestone area near Pamplona, with slabs, crimps, overhangs and more than 800 routes from 4a to 9a.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body:
Etxauri is one of Navarra's important limestone climbing areas, close enough to Pamplona to work as a practical base but serious enough to deserve its own destination page. The climbing is technical, varied and strongly tied to route reading rather than pure fitness.

It is a good choice when you want Spanish limestone without the full winter-canyon scene of the Valencia areas. Autumn and spring are the clean planning windows, with summer heat kept out of the main recommendation.

sections.heading: Rock and climbing character
sections.body:
The climbing is on limestone, with slabs, crimps, technical walls and overhanging faces. The style rewards footwork and body position, especially on the less steep routes.

Treat Etxauri mainly as a sport-climbing destination, but leave room in the plan for longer routes and a more traditional cliff feel than a pure roadside sport venue.

sections.heading: Who it suits
sections.body:
Etxauri suits climbers who like technical limestone and want a broad grade spread close to a city base. The low grades make mileage possible, while the upper end reaches serious sport climbing.

It is not the best fit if the group only wants soft beginner cragging. The useful message is technical climbing first, convenience second.

sections.heading: Grades and difficulty
sections.body: The supported scale is more than 800 routes from 4a to 9a. That is broad enough for mixed groups, provided route choice accounts for the area's technical style.

sections.heading: Season and conditions
sections.body: Autumn and spring are the recommended windows. Summer heat is the main avoid flag, especially on exposed limestone.

sections.heading: Gear and equipment
sections.body: Bring standard sport gear, a helmet and enough route information to choose sectors by aspect. No special destination gear beyond normal limestone sport climbing was verified in this batch.
warnings: No sourced gear and equipment content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Transport and access
sections.body: Etxauri sits close to Pamplona, but a rented car is more practical than relying on public transport. It gives better control over sectors, timing and heat management.

sections.heading: Where to stay
sections.body:
Pamplona is the practical base for most Etxauri trips, with city accommodation, food and rest-day options close enough to keep logistics simple.

There are campsites in the wider Pamplona area, but treat exact lodging choice as a planning step rather than something to solve at the cliff.

sections.heading: Rest days
sections.body: Pamplona gives the easiest rest-day base: food, city wandering and logistics without turning the climbing trip into a long transfer day.
warnings: No sourced rest days content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Practical tips
sections.body: Use the first day to learn the rock rather than chasing numbers. Technical limestone grades can feel sharper when the footholds are small and the wall is less forgiving than it looks.
warnings: No sourced practical tips content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Safety notes
sections.body: Heat and technical fatigue are the main practical issues. Start with conservative objectives, especially if arriving from a different style of climbing.
